tasks.commitBody:
The Links page shipped with no page shell and nobody noticed until a human opened it on a phone — twice, across two commits. The control-class guard closed this gap one level down; this closes it for the page itself: every route's +page.svelte either contains the house shell — the exact string library, admin, profile and roster carry — or appears on an explicit allowlist with its reason written inline where the next reader meets it. A new route is a violation until someone gives it the shell or writes its line; the allowlist is the chokepoint, and it fails closed.

The check asserts presence, not structure, and says so in its header: roster declares snippet blocks before its root and the agenda's root is conditional, so a root-element check would false-fail two of thirteen routes, and a guard that is wrong about two routes gets switched off. Presence is exactly strong enough for the defect that happened — Links had the shell nowhere. The checker strips HTML comments before matching, the lesson both of this week's real sweeps taught, so a commented-out shell satisfies nothing.

The instrument is pinned the way this family now pins instruments: an exported pure function whose behavior lives in committed inline-string fixtures — the removed-shell case, the fail-closed unlisted-route case, the allowlisted-without-shell case — never in counts over the tree the next fix will change; the live revert-one-conformer proof ran at RED time and was restored byte-identically. Six exceptions, each with its accurate reason — including that the centered auth/invite family's true discriminator is the absent py-10, two of its four members carrying px-6 — and the dependencies:{} sibling question stays deferred to its own slice, its assertion already living in the workers fences.

Closes #341
